definitions.gloss: nice to meet you, please treat me well
definitions.explanation: Used when meeting someone for the first time, often after はじめまして. Full form is よろしくお{願|ねが}いします.
Used when asking someone to do something or take care of something.
Used when asking someone to pass along greetings.

examples.japanese: はじめまして。{田中|たなか}です。よろしく。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. I'm Tanaka. Pleased to meet you.

examples.japanese: よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Thank you in advance. / Pleased to meet you.

examples.japanese: お{母|かあ}さんにもよろしく{言|い}ってね。
examples.english: Please give my regards to your mother too.

examples.japanese: この{件|けん}はよろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Please take care of this matter.

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}もどうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I look forward to your continued support next year as well.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}からお{世話|せわ}になります。よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: I'll be in your care from today. Nice to meet you.

examples.japanese: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}の{佐藤|さとう}です。よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I'm Sato, a new employee. Pleased to meet you.
Looking forward to our future relationship!

examples.japanese: {予約|よやく}の{件|けん}、よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Please take care of the reservation matter.

examples.japanese: お{手伝|てつだ}いのほど、よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
{ご家族|ごかぞく}にもよろしく。
examples.english: Please give my regards to your family as well.

examples.japanese: {皆様|みなさま}によろしくお{伝|つた}えください。
examples.english: Please give my regards to everyone.

examples.japanese: {山田|やまだ}さんによろしく{伝|つた}えてください。
examples.english: Please give my regards to Mr. Yamada.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}によろしくお{伝|つた}えいただけますか。
examples.english: Could you please give my regards to the senior?

examples.japanese: {今後|こんご}ともよろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: I look forward to working with you in the future.

notes:
よろしく is an extremely versatile expression derived from the adjective よろしい (good, fine).

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- よろしく: casual
- よろしくお{願|ねが}いします: polite
- よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします: humble/very polite

USAGE CONTEXTS:
1. Introductions: はじめまして、よろしくお{願|ねが}いします
2. Requests: この{件|けん}、よろしくお{願|ねが}いします
3. Passing regards: {田中|たなか}さんによろしく
4. Email closings: {今後|こんご}ともよろしくお{願|ねが}いします

COMMON MISTAKE:
よろしく cannot be directly translated. Its meaning depends entirely on context - it's closer to a social lubricant than a single English phrase.
